chapter: Radio, Jazz Record and Blue Note (Reel 2)
title: Running Village jam sessions in a loft, 1943-44
summary: After the radio, Hodes ran jam sessions in a Village loft at a dollar a head. He lists the players he had.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But he objected. So I lost the job. But in that time, I gained an audience, and I started running jam sessions in the Village. And we found a place that was just perfect for us. Seats that would slant up. And -- yes, theater type of thing, but it was actually a loft. And the -- a dollar apiece to get in. $20 for the leader, me, $10 for the men, by anybody who wanted.
My gosh, I don't know who I didn't have.

This was '43, '44. Okay, Mezz, Pee Wee Russell, Rod Cless, I had all three. Trumpets, Max Kaminsky, Muggsy Spanier, Fred Allen, drums, George Wettling, or Freddy Moore or Kaiser Marshall, whoever was available. And Pops Foster always on bass.
